objective.text: Name a card's three statuses in order and what earns each.

body.general: How do you really learn a card? Each card teaches one idea [f1]. Keep it open for a moment, and it counts as Read [f2]. Pass its Check, every question right in one go, and it is Understood [f3]. Then explain it out loud and compare with the model answer: that is Can explain [f4]. Try it lets you turn the 3D embryo and scrub through the days [f5]. Lessons take each chapter card by card [f11]. Your Remember deck brings the card's prompts back 1 day later, then 3, then 7 days apart [f6].
body.mbbs: Each card teaches one idea and opens with what you will be able to do [f1]. Keeping a card open for a moment marks it Read [f2]. Its Check tests that objective; every question right in one run marks it Understood [f3]. Explaining it aloud, then comparing with the model answer, marks it Can explain [f4]. Try it opens the card's 3D scene: turn it and scrub the days; Open full 3D adds slicing [f5]. The card's Remember prompts join your deck once you read it [f6]. They come back 1 day later, then 3, then 7 days apart while you get them right [f6]. Today shows how many prompts are due and offers two plans, On the go and Study [f7]. Lessons take each chapter card by card, in sittings of up to 15 minutes [f11]. Mixed review asks Check questions from cards you marked Understood, with the card text hidden [f12]. The small numbers after a sentence open its facts, each with a source and a confidence mark [f8].

facts.text: Each card teaches one idea and opens with what you will be able to do.
A card counts as Read once it has been open for a moment (1.5 s).
Getting every question of a card's Check right in one run marks the card Understood.
After Understood, you explain the idea out loud and compare with a model answer to mark it Can explain.
Try it shows the card's 3D scene, which you can turn and scrub through the days; Open full 3D adds slicing.
A card's Remember prompts join your deck when you read it. They come back 1 day later, then 3, then every 7 days while you get them right.
Today shows how many Remember prompts are due and offers two plans: On the go, up to 5 minutes, and Study, 15–30 minutes.
The small number after a sentence opens the facts behind it, each with its source and confidence mark.
Lessons take a chapter card by card in sittings of up to 15 minutes: read, Check, the 3D where the card has one, then Remember.
Mixed review asks Check questions from cards you have understood, mixed across chapters, with the card text hidden. It never changes a card's status.
Watch it will link each card to its episode; until episodes exist it says Coming soon.
A missed prompt that was due comes back the next day and starts its spacing again. Any miss also repeats once at the end of that session.

misconceptions.wrong: Once you have read a card, you have learned it.
misconceptions.right: Read is only the first status: pass the Check, then explain it in your own words.

checks.prompt: Put a card's three statuses in order, first to last.
checks.why: Each status needs the one before it.

options: Every Check question right in one run
Keeping the card open a while
checks.why: Keeping a card open makes it Read; only a clean run of the whole Check makes it Understood.

options: Explaining it aloud, then comparing with the model answer
Passing the Check a second time
Opening the card a second time
checks.why: Can explain comes from explaining the idea in your own words and checking it against the model answer.

remember.q: What are a card's three statuses, in order?

remember.a: Every Check question right in one run [f3].

remember.q: When do Remember prompts come back?
remember.a: 1 day after you read the card, then 3, then 7 days apart while you get them right [f6].
